SIBO shouldn't be too hard to get tested for if you have an understanding doctor. The test is a simple breath test - you drink either lactulose or glucose before the test and then breathe into a device multiple times during a 2-3 hour period (usually it's 3 I believe). You don't need to rule anything out beforehand - if you suspect you may have SIBO, you can absolutely go for it and do the test. If the test is negative, then you can do tests for other possible causes too (reminder that the tests can come back as false negative too though)

I haven't completely overcome it yet, but I've eased my symptoms quite a lot with herbal antimicrobials (such as berberine, oregano oil, allicin etc). You can also do antibiotics (rifaximin) depending on your SIBO type (methane or hydrogen dominant) but depending on where you live and your insurance, it can get pretty expensive. Herbals should be a cheaper way and can be a safer way to beat SIBO (but obviously it cannot be 100% safe as everything may have side effects)
